newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday December 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday December 20.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Former prime minister and opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi was questioned for eight hours by magistrates who are looking into alleged irregularities by Antonio Di Pietro, former anti-graft hero and ex-Public Works minister (all).

* The parliamentary lower house is expected to examine today a controversial law proposal which would reduce sanctions for illicit parties' financing, but leftist PDS party and far-right National Alliance want to avoid an "amnisty" for past offences. The PDS is the major party in the centre-left government coalition (all).
* Italian movie legend Marcello Mastroianni died at his home in Paris, aged 72 (all).
* Metalworkers unions called a two-hour strike for today as talks with employers federation Federmeccanica collapsed for the third time in a bitter dispute over contracts (all).
* After CPI data from four sample cities, the increase in consumer prices in December is seen at 2.6 percent year-on-year, the same level of November (all).
* British-based Airtours and U.S. Carnival Corp announced a 181 billion pound joint offer for 100 percent of Italian cruise line operator Costa Crociere (all).

* State industrial holding IRI approved the transfer of shares in motorway operator Autostrade from 100 percent-owned unit Fintecna to itself, preparing for the sell-off of Autostrade expected by June 1997. The decision to de-merge the company from Fintecna, which held some 66.2 percent of the firm, means that IRI will receive all the proceeds from its eventual privatisation (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
